text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a focused bakeoff comparing SmoothQuant-lite + activation-balancing vs AWQ-mix + GPTQ on longctx workloads (48k and 64k). results look different than I expected.

sanjay: nice, what model and dataset?

maya: model = open-opt-13b-clone (our adapter stack). eval suite = longbench-chat-50 (mix of code, docs, and long dialogues). perf axis = perplexity delta on heldout plus pass@1 for code snippets, and token-latency profile.

olivia: short summary numbers pls

maya: sure — 48k context:
- SmoothQuant-lite int8: +0.9% ppl vs fp16 baseline, pass@1 -0.6 pts
- AWQ-mix int8 (act-aware): +1.6% ppl, pass@1 -1.8 pts
- GPTQ fp8 hybrid: +0.4% ppl, pass@1 -0.2 pts

64k context:
- SmoothQuant-lite int8: +1.8% ppl, pass@1 -1.0 pts
- AWQ-mix int8: +3.2% ppl, pass@1 -3.5 pts (big regression on long code traces)
- GPTQ fp8 hybrid: +0.6% ppl, pass@1 -0.4 pts

liam: interesting — AWQ double-digit degradation at 64k? do you see KV-cache corruption or activation saturation?

maya: not corruption per se, more like gradual drift in attention scores leading to hallucination on code blocks after ~48k tokens. profiler shows activation norms spike around layer 18 onwards. attaching snippet from the run.

bench-bot: uploaded file longctx-1855001234/profiler/actnorms.csv

maya: config I used for repeatability:
```
run: sq-actbalanced-longctx-2026
model: open-opt-13b-clone
quant: smoothquant-lite-int8
activation-balancing: true
evals: longbench-chat-50
context_sizes: [48000, 64000]
batch_size: 1
seq_bucket: dynamic
profiling: true
```

sanjay: can you try SmoothQuant with a small activation clamp (alpha=0.6) and AWQ with fallback int8-matmul-fallback at runtime? maybe AWQ's block quant is amplifying scale drift.

maya: on it. initial smoke run: applying act-clamp alpha=0.6 on top of SmoothQuant-lite reduces 64k ppl delta to +0.9% and pass@1 drop to -0.3 pts. AWQ + fallback (matmul fallback for layers 16-22) improves but still worse than sq+clamp. will run full eval overnight.

olivia: great — do we have a perf/cost tradeoff table? latency and tokens/sec at 64k are important for deployment.

maya: approximate throughput on A100-80Gb:
- sq-int8: 72 tokens/sec (steady), median latency per request 1.1s for first 1k tokens and then ~0.9s/sec chunk
- awq-int8 (no fallback): 86 tokens/sec but tail latency variance huge once seq>50k, often spikes 3-6x
- gptq-fp8: 95 tokens/sec but memory knee requires kv-eviction after ~56k unless we pin memory

liam: that throughput ordering is surprising vs quality. gptq fp8 looks tempting but memory management is risky for Dedicated.

maya: notes on deploy profile: for Dedicated we prefer consistent latency (sq-int8+clamp looks best). For Hosted API we can offer gptq-fp8 with aggressive kv-compact -> better cost but occasional retries.

sanjay: do we have a checklist to onboard these variants? especially quant mapping and fallback policy.

maya: adding quick checklist here:
1) quant artifact + checksum
2) per-layer scale table
3) act-balance metadata (alpha, per-layer thresholds)
4) runtime fallback policy (layers to matmul fallback, kv-compact thresholds)
5) eval bundle (longbench-chat-50 results + pass@k)
6) perf profile (throughput, tail latency, memory knee)

olivia: can you upload the full eval tar and tag the model MR? i'll review tomorrow and add to the catalog if sq+clamp keeps stable in overnight run.

maya: will do. tagging @sanjay for follow-up on AWQ fallback policy. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks — ping me when full logs are up.

maya: done — uploaded tar gz at https://redwood.internal/runs/1855001234/longctx-bake.tar.gz and pinned logs in the run page.
